## How they got there
Real Madrid secured the title by beating Liverpool 1-0 in the final after navigating through 16 knockout teams during the 2021-22 season. Their profile was defined by exceptional control and discipline, as they were better than 100% of that season's group-phase teams in passes per game with a value of 670, while also ranking higher than 97% of their peers in pre-season UEFA club coefficient points at 127.0 and fouls committed per game at just 7.8.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Real Madrid as a primary finalist, noting that they ranked 5th among knockout teams despite an 18.8% probability of reaching the final compared to a base rate of 12.5%. Although their statistical profile placed them outside the model's top two choices, the expected outcome aligns with the semi-finals on the prediction scale, which sits at 2.06 stages away from elimination before the quarter-finals.

## Weak spots
The team displayed clear areas where they beat fewer opponents than average, specifically in long passes (% of passes) where they were better than only 6% of that season's teams with a value of 8.8. They also struggled relative to peers in distance covered per game at 110.3 km, beating just 12% of the group-phase teams, and opponent shots per game (lower is better) where they were superior to only 44% of their counterparts with a value of 9.0.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
